results.correct_value: About 9,400 ft of gain (and loss) car to car; itinerary days 5,600/350, 3,450/3,450, 350/5,600
results.evidence: A 2022 ascent via the North Fork Sauk trail, PCT and Foam Creek trail logged 33 miles and 9,400 ft of gain. A guided itinerary on the same approach sums to about 9,000 ft of gain (1,000 + 3,800 + 4,200) over about 30 miles. The itinerary's 7,750 ft is physically impossible: trailhead (2,050 ft) to summit (10,541 ft) is already 8,491 ft net, and day 1 (2,050 to 7,300 ft) and day 2 (7,300 to 10,541 ft) were each below their own net rise. gain_ft/loss_ft 9,400 are kept; itinerary days, totalNote and the summit-day figure in the approach prose are brought to it (split follows the topography: 5,250 ft net to Glacier Gap plus the drop into the White Chuck basin; 3,241 ft net camp-to-summit plus the drop onto Gerdine Ridge).

results.fact: dist_km (~9 mi) vs itinerary round-trip total (~21-25 mi)
results.evidence: dist_km 14.5 km = 9.0 mi is the one-way distance to the Boulder Basin high camp (itinerary days 1+2 = 7 + 2 mi; the route description gives about 9 miles to Boulder Basin), while the itinerary total adds the summit day and the hike out. Both depend on the White Chuck approach, whose validity is the separate unresolved trailhead contradiction.

results.fact: Structured waypoints/road/approach_logistics describe a different trailhead than the approach/itinerary prose
results.correct_value: The White Chuck approach the prose describes is no longer usable; current access is from the North Fork Sauk trailhead via White Pass and the PCT, which the waypoints/road/approach_logistics already reflect
results.evidence: The Forest Service page for White Chuck River Trail 643 lists it as 'INACCESSIBLE, NO ROAD OR TRAIL ACCESS', washed away by the 2003 flood, less than a third remaining and no plans to repair. A 2020 party found FR 23 blocked by boulders, walked the old road and lost the trail at Pumice Creek. So the approach, itinerary days 1, 2 and 4, itinerary.cal, timing.sectionBreakdown, descent_text, approach_variants (White Chuck marked primary) and the bivy entries describe a defunct approach while the waypoints (coordinates cannot change) start at North Fork Sauk. The fix is a full rewrite of approach narrative, mileages, hours and gains for the North Fork Sauk -> White Pass -> PCT north -> Sitkum Creek -> Boulder Basin line; no source consulted gives those segment distances, so no patch was written. Also note the 'Boulder Basin Camp' waypoint pin sits at 48.105,-121.13, east of the summit rather than in Boulder Basin (pin position out of scope).
